unit.title: Subjunctive: emotions & reactions
unit.subtitle: React with feeling: me alegro de que, es una lástima que, siento que

grammar.title: When your feelings react to someone else
grammar.intro: You already flip verbs to the subjunctive after quiero que and espero que. The same thing happens whenever you react emotionally to what someone else does. Being glad, sorry, annoyed, or moved — if there's a feeling plus que plus a different subject, the second verb goes subjunctive.

sections.heading: Emotion + que + subjunctive
sections.body: The pattern is: [emotion] + que + [subjunctive verb]. Your feeling is the trigger; the person you're reacting to is the second subject.

ex.en: It bothers me that you arrive late.

sections.heading: The irregulars you'll reuse forever
sections.body: A handful of verbs have irregular subjunctive stems. You'll meet these constantly, so memorise them now:

ex.es: Es una lástima que no tengas tiempo.
ex.en: It's a shame you don't have time.
I like that you're so kind.

sections.heading: Same person? Use the infinitive
sections.body: The subjunctive only appears when the two subjects are different. If you feel something about your own action, drop the que and use the plain infinitive.

takeaways: Me alegro de que, me gusta que, es una lástima que, siento que, me molesta que.
Reuse the irregulars: sea, esté, tenga, vaya, haga.
Same subject? Skip que and use the infinitive: Me alegro de estar aquí.

mistakes.w: Me alegro de que estás aquí.
mistakes.r: Me alegro de que estés aquí.
mistakes.why: After an emotion + que, use the subjunctive (estés), not the indicative (estás).

mistakes.w: Me alegro de que yo esté aquí.
mistakes.why: With the same subject, drop the que and use the infinitive.

mistakes.w: Es una lástima que no tienes tiempo.
mistakes.r: Es una lástima que no tengas tiempo.
mistakes.why: tener flips to the subjunctive after this expression: tengas, not tienes.

exercises.prompt: Me alegro de que tú ___ aquí.
exercises.no: After an emotion + que, use the subjunctive: “estés”.

exercises.prompt: Es una lástima que no ___ venir.
exercises.prompt_en: It's a shame you can't come.
exercises.no: After 'es una lástima que', use the subjunctive: “puedas”.

exercises.ok: ¡Perfecto! Me alegro de que estés — subjuntivo.
exercises.no: “Me alegro de que estés aquí” — estar flips to estés.

exercises.prompt_en: It bothers me that you arrive late.

exercises.prompt: Match each infinitive to its subjunctive (yo/él) form.
exercises.ok: ¡Excelente! You've locked in the key irregulars.

exercises.no: It was: “Siento que estés enfermo.” (I'm sorry you're sick.)
